subject: Dedicated capacity sizing call - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@cloudops.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing call - next steps

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the productive discovery session this morning. Recap / open items we discussed: 
- You're planning to move inference workloads to a dedicated capacity pool for predictable latency and cost.
- Primary use case: customer chat + ticket summarization with occasional batch embedding jobs for search.
- Key questions for sizing: expected peak concurrency, average request/response token counts, QPS by endpoint, and latency SLOs.

Next step: let's schedule a 45-minute dedicated capacity sizing call (we'll bring a solutions engineer) to walk through throughput/latency requirements and a preliminary sizing worksheet. Can you confirm availability for any of these times (PT):
- Thu Mar 12, 10:00-10:45am PT
- Thu Mar 12, 3:00-3:45pm PT
- Fri Mar 13, 9:00-9:45am PT

If it's helpful, please paste a quick table with expected peak QPS, average prompt tokens, average generated tokens, and any batch/ingest windows — that will let David come prepared with a draft capacity calc. I've attached a short agenda and our sizing workbook (capacity_calc_v1.xlsx).

Agenda highlights (attached PDF):
1) Quick context and traffic profile (5 min)
2) Throughput & latency targets by route (15 min)
3) Sizing walk-through & options (20 min)
4) Next steps & timelines (5 min)

Thanks — looking forward to locking this in.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood_sizing-agenda.pdf, capacity_calc_v1.xlsx

From: Alice Nguyen <alice@cloudops.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir.rao@cloudops.com>
Date: 2026-03-11T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing call - next steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and the workbook. We're available for the Thu Mar 12 3:00pm PT slot — that works best for our infra lead. Quick answers to your sizing ask below (high level):

- Use cases / endpoints:
  * Chat completions (primary): expected peak ~5 req/s sustained per region, with spikes to ~12 req/s for short bursts. Average prompt size ~450 tokens, average generated tokens ~220 tokens.
  * Ticket summarization (async): expected 15-20 jobs/min, average total tokens processed per job ~900 tokens (mostly generation-heavy).
  * Embeddings (batch & search): nightly batch: ~250k records over a 3-hour window; realtime search embeddings ~3 req/s.

- Concurrency / latency targets:
  * Target p95 latency for chat completions: <= 700ms.
  * Ticket summarization: p95 <= 2s acceptable for most jobs.
  * Embeddings: < 500ms for realtime, batch is flexible.

- Traffic notes: we expect to start with one region (us-west) and expand later. Data residency: logs can be sent to your hosted observability; we'll request standard SOC2 artifacts during procurement.

I've attached our internal infra checklist that includes VPC/peering notes. Please include David (solutions engineer) on the call — he can walk the worksheet.

Thanks,
Alice Nguyen
Head of ML Platforms, CloudOps Inc.
alice@cloudops.com
(510) 555-0987

Attachments: cloudops_infra_checklist.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-11T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing call - next steps

Perfect — thanks for the details, Alice. Locked in Thu Mar 12, 3:00-3:45pm PT. I've sent a calendar invite with a Zoom link (see related_links).

David, can you prepare a draft sizing sheet using Alice's numbers (peak bursts, avg tokens, nightly batch) and be ready to walk through two config options: (A) single-region reserved pool with burst capacity, (B) single-region reserved + burst to hosted. Please also bring a quick note on expected cost delta and latency implications for each.

Rachel, I'll include pre-call materials to the invite and loop in procurement if we start contract talks after the sizing call.

Alice — if you have an RFx or internal procurement questions ahead of time, feel free to attach them here.

Thanks all — see you Thu.

Cheers,
Marissa
